title: Tool: Claude Code hook config generator
description:
New interactive tool at /tools/claude-hook-builder/ (slug: claude-hook-builder). Purpose: user picks Claude Code lifecycle events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Notification, PreCompact) and an intent per event (block command, validate file edits, run formatter, inject context, log/audit), fills in matcher + command fields, and the tool renders a ready-to-paste hooks block for .claude/settings.json plus a copy button.

FEATURES: (a) event picker with one-line explanation of when each event fires and what exit codes/JSON output mean for it (exit 2 blocks on PreToolUse; stdout JSON with decision/reason; hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext for UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart); (b) per-hook rows: matcher (tool name regex for PreToolUse/PostToolUse, empty = all), command, timeout; (c) live JSON preview pane (pretty-printed, syntax-highlight optional via plain <pre>); (d) preset recipes: block-dangerous-bash, format-on-edit, protect-paths, session-context-injector, audit-log; (e) copy-to-clipboard and download settings.json snippet.

DATA MODEL: {schemaVersion:1, hooks: Array<{event, matcher, command, timeout?}>} -> serialize to the settings.json hooks shape {hooks: {EventName: [{matcher, hooks:[{type: command, command, timeout}]}]}}.

title: Tool: scrobble / listening stats visualizer
description:
New interactive tool at /tools/scrobble-stats/ (slug: scrobble-stats). Purpose: paste or drop a Last.fm CSV export or a ListenBrainz JSON export and get listening-stats charts — fully client-side, file never leaves the browser (say so in the hero).

FEATURES: (a) intake: file drop + paste textarea; detect format: ListenBrainz JSON export (array or {listens:[...]} with listened_at + track_metadata.artist_name/track_name/release_name) and generic scrobble CSV with columns like artist,album,track,date (e.g. from lastfm-to-csv exporters) — parse both defensively, show detected format + row count, friendly error otherwise; write a tiny CSV parser inline (handle quoted fields), NO papaparse dependency; (b) charts, all inline SVG, no chart library: top artists bar chart (top 15), listens-per-month bar timeline, listens-by-hour-of-day histogram, listens-by-weekday; (c) stat tiles: total listens, unique artists, unique tracks, busiest day; (d) time-range filter (all/last year/last 90 days); (e) copy summary as markdown. Cap parsing at 100k rows with a truncation notice. Persist NOTHING but UI prefs — do not put listen data in localStorage (large).

DATA MODEL (in-memory): {listens:[{ts,artist,track,album}]} normalized from either format.

CROSS-LINK: posts src/content/posts/2026-08-12-homelab-music-recommendations-field-guide.md and 2026-08-12-youtube-to-scrobble.md.

title: Tool: PO responsibility split by team size (RACI sketcher)
description:
New interactive tool at /tools/po-responsibility-map/ (slug: po-responsibility-map). Purpose: interactive companion to the post about what a product owner absorbs vs hands off as team size changes — pick your team shape, get a responsibility map, then adjust it into a lightweight RACI you can export.

FEATURES: (a) inputs: team size slider (2-30 eng), toggles for has dedicated BA, has PM above PO, has UX researcher, number of teams; (b) responsibility list (~18 rows seeded from the posts: discovery interviews, backlog ordering, acceptance review, stakeholder updates, OKR drafting, sprint planning, spec writing, analytics review, support triage, roadmap comms, pricing input, release notes, demo hosting, experiment design, user-story slicing, dependency wrangling, hiring input, marketing research) — each row gets a computed default owner (PO absorbs / delegate / shared) from simple threshold rules keyed to the inputs (encode the rules as a plain data table in the component, e.g. above 8 eng delegate spec writing to leads; with BA present move analytics review to BA); (c) every computed cell is user-overridable via a select; overridden cells get an edited dot; (d) summary strip: N absorbed / N delegated / N shared + a warning when absorbed exceeds ~8 rows (spread too thin); (e) export markdown table copy button.

title: Tool: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md linter
description:
New interactive tool at /tools/agents-md-linter/ (slug: agents-md-linter). Purpose: paste a CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md agent-instructions file and get heuristic checks — fully client-side, NO LLM calls, NO network.

CHECKS to implement (each returns pass/warn/fail + message + line refs): (a) length: warn over 300 lines or 12k chars, fail over 40k chars — long files dilute instruction-following; (b) structure: has headings, has a commands section (looks for fenced code with pnpm/npm/make/cargo etc.), has a project-description opening paragraph; (c) contradiction sniff: flags pairs of lines that both match a curated pattern list with opposite polarity (always X vs never X on same keyword — keep simple keyword match, list ~10 patterns like commit/push/test/format); (d) vague-language detector: flags lines with try to, if possible, be careful, as appropriate, generally — instructions should be testable; (e) duplication: near-identical lines repeated (normalized string compare); (f) TODO/stale markers; (g) secrets sniff: obvious API-key patterns. Score 0-100 from weighted checks with a summary badge.

UI: big textarea (or file drop using FileReader), Run lint button, results list grouped by severity with line numbers, score badge. Persist last input to localStorage.

CROSS-LINK: no single perfect post; link the tools footer only, and mention in description that it pairs with agent-setup content.

2. Island: src/components/tools/<slug>/ — React 19 + TypeScript components. NO new npm dependencies, NO framer-motion, NO CSS-in-JS. Style only with the Tailwind utilities and token variables already used by existing tools — mirror class usage from src/components/tools/spec-builder/SpecBuilder.tsx and src/components/tools/okr-check-in/CheckInTool.tsx. Tokens live in src/styles/tokens.css; never hardcode colors or px values.
3. Persist all state to localStorage (JSON, versioned shape with a schemaVersion field), same approach as existing tools.
4. Register the tool: add a footer link in src/components/chrome/SiteFooter.astro following the existing /tools/ list-item markup around lines 78-162.
5. SEO: SiteShell title ends with — Free Tool and description is a full keyword-rich sentence mirroring okr-check-in.astro.
6. Validate: pnpm check and pnpm build must pass. URL shape /tools/<slug>/ is permanent once shipped.
Cross-link rule: when linking a blog post, find it in src/content/posts/, read its directory frontmatter — the URL is /<directory>/<slug>/ (or /<slug>/ if no directory). Add a link from the tool hero to the post AND a short callout with a link from the post body to the tool.
